title: Probe-scout weekly brief: quant onboarding & eval catch-up
content:
Week: 2027-06-07 weekly capture (probe-scout group)
Attendees: Asha, Miguel, Leah, Owen, Samir (sync + async notes consolidated)
Purpose: quick snapshot of ongoing quant onboarding experiments, small eval runs, and short-term rollout decisions. Focus on anomalies (latency tails, eval regressions) and next steps for an internal canary.

1) Quick summary / headlines
- Small-model 4-bit quant (GPTQ-style) showed promising cost reduction but a subtle accuracy regression on the synthetic instruction-eval set (BLEU-like proxy down ~2.3 absolute on long-answer split).
- KV-cache eviction pattern observed when microbatching > 8 across concurrent streams on dedicated-dev cluster — increases p99 latency by ~35ms in the worst cases.
- Embedding drift test (anchor set vs. live prompts) shows minor cosine drift after quantized model onboarding; likely due to rounding in final layer norm.
- Canary plan draft: start canary on Dedicated pool with traffic cap 5% and automatic fallback to full-precision variant on quality regression > 1.5 point metric or latency SLO breach.

2) Experiments run this week (short lab notes)
- exp-q4gptq-v2 (A100-80GB, single node)
  - config: GPTQ-style post-training quantization, 4-bit, per-channel, outlier clipping 0.995
  - batch distribution: sequence length median 128, 95th perc 640 (synthetic load)
  - perf: throughput +2.6x tokens/s vs FP16; mean latency per request (seq=128) ~ 42ms (FP16 110ms), p99 320ms
  - quality: instruction-eval microbench (200 prompts): accuracy proxy 86.7% vs FP16 baseline 89.0% (diff -2.3) — failure modes concentrated in long reasoning steps where token-generation diverges after 200 tokens.
  - notes: try softer clipping and small fine-tune with 512 prompt snippets to recover divergence.

- exp-int8-lc (A100 multi-GPU)
  - config: int8 dynamic quant (layerwise symmetric), MHA kernel rewrites enabled
  - perf: +1.8x tokens/s, latency tail improved relative to q4 (p99 210ms)
  - quality: negligible delta on short QA set, small drift on embeddings (mean cosine drop 0.006)
  - notes: promising for embedding workloads; candidate for embedding-on-dedicated path.

- kv-microbatch-stress-21
  - config: 12 concurrent streams, microbatch size 12, KV cache TTL default
  - observation: after ~18 minutes sustained, observed KV eviction log warnings on the node (LRU thrash) and p99 latency spikes +35ms; pattern reproduced on dev-dedicated-3 cluster
  - hypothesis: our KV cache sharding heuristics under-estimate memory pressure when microbatching and many concurrent short sessions occur; eviction threshold calculation needs to account for active stream count.
  - mitigation tested: lowering per-stream microbatch to 6 reduces p99 spike to +8ms; not a full fix.

3) Evals and metrics (detailed)
- Synthetic instruction-eval (200 prompts, split short/long)
  - FP16 baseline: short 92.1, long 89.0 (overall 90.6)
  - q4gptq-v2: short 90.4, long 86.7 (overall 88.6)
  - int8-lc: short 91.8, long 88.9 (overall 90.3)
  - Implication: q4 impacts long-form generative coherence more than int8; explore hybrid routing (int8 for long outputs) or fallback policy for long sequences.

- Embedding drift check (anchor set 5k vectors)
  - FP16 vs q4gptq-v2: mean cosine 0.992 (drift 0.008), downstream retrieval top-1 recall drop 0.7% absolute
  - for int8-lc: mean cosine 0.994 (drift 0.006), recall drop 0.3% absolute
  - Note: drift is small but noticeable for high-precision retrieval tasks — consider per-customer QA thresholds.

4) Onboarding checklist status for model candidate 'redwood-small-x' (quant candidate)
- PRs: quant conversion tooling in PR #142 (linked)
- Unit tests: tokenization + sample-decoder-tests ✓, long-seq stress tests △ (failing tail-case) -> tracked in MLPROBE-58
- Eval harness: integration with Canary pipeline partial (canary trigger + rollback hooks implemented) ✓
- Observability: added token-level cost breakdown but missing per-request quality deltas in console — action item to add the eval delta trace to request logs (see action items).

5) Anomalies, blockers, and open questions
- Anomaly A: occasional truncation of generated outputs when switching from q4 to int8 on the same session. Hypothesis: incompatible KV cache key encoding between kernels. Repro steps and logs attached to PR; need kernel-engineer pairing session.
- Blocker B: cannot recreate the long-answer divergence locally with small seeds; seems dataset-dependent (conversation history length compounds the drift). Need a reproducible small dataset that can trigger divergence within 20–40 tokens. Leah to attempt synthetic generation of failing seeds.
- Question C: rollout criteria thresholds — suggested metric thresholds for canary auto-rollback: quality drop > 1.5 points on primary eval OR p99 latency increase > 20% above baseline OR error rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes. Are these conservative enough? Ops asked to sign off.

6) Decisions made (quick)
- Proceed with a limited canary on Dedicated with traffic cap 5% and auto-fallback to FP16 variant on the three rollback conditions above (pending Ops confirmation).
- Prefer int8 for embedding-only workloads initially; keep q4 candidate behind canary for text-generation workloads until long-answer regression addressed.

7) Action items (owners + due)
- Leah: create a synthetic seed corpus that reproduces long-answer divergence and post to MLPROBE-58 (due 2027-06-10).
- Miguel + Owen: schedule kernel pairing to inspect KV cache key encoding and microbatch interaction (meeting by 2027-06-09).
- Asha: add eval-delta tracing to request logs and a lightweight per-request quality score tag for canary (PR draft by 2027-06-11).
- Samir: run softer-clipping q4 variant (clip 0.997 + small fine-tune with 512 snippets) and push results to the experiment dashboard (by 2027-06-12).
- Team: Ops to confirm rollback thresholds and add to canary runbook (Ops owner: TBD, due 2027-06-10).

8) Notes to self / rough ideas (brainstorm fragments)
- Hybrid routing rule idea: if expected output length > 300 tokens, route to int8 fallback if available, else FP16; reduces user-visible regressions but needs routing cost accounting.
- Consider microcache layer: per-conversation microcache that keeps a small local KV for hot short sessions to reduce global KV thrash. Implementation complexity moderate.
- Metric to monitor: token divergence index — compare n-gram overlap of generated continuations vs FP16 baseline in first 50 tokens; good signal for early rollback.

9) Next sync agenda (2027-06-14)
- Leah demo: failing seed reproduction + short triage
- Miguel/Owen: kernel findings + KV eviction action plan
- Samir: q4 softer-clipping results + decision on small fine-tune
- Ops: confirm rollback thresholds and add to canary runbook

Appendix: logs and short snippets (copied here for quick reference)
- Example divergence excerpt (prompt id 3749): FP16: "...and therefore the proof concludes that X is necessary." | q4gptq-v2: "...so the proof is done. The conclusion is that Y." (semantic flip after 42 tokens)
- Observed KV eviction log sample: "WARN kv_cache: evict shard=5 reason=mem_pressure active_streams=12 microbatch=12"

If anything missing or you want deeper export of the run dashboard, ping me in #applied-ml-probe.

End of brief.
